lemma.note: cq1 scan 5: OIr. día 'day' (weekday names, día brátha, cach día). Kaikki Old Irish día 'day' < Proto-Celtic *dyīus < *dyew-; Matasović EDPC p0107 s.v. *diyw-o- 'day' (PIE *diy-ew-, paradigm *diyews / *diywos); lexicon *dyḗws lists Proto-Celtic *dyīus. Not día 'god'.
cq1 scan 5: día 'God' before nime / uilechumachtach / mór / dúileach / na ndúl. Kaikki Old Irish día 'god' < Proto-Celtic *deiwos < *deywós; not *dyḗws 'sky'.

cq1 scan 6: meinic / menic 'often, frequent'. Matasović EDPC p0279 s.v. *menekki- 'frequent, abundant' < PIE *men- (IEW 730), cognate Go. manags, OCS mъnogъ; Kaikki Proto-Celtic *menekkis gives *menegʰ- or a substrate word and calls the *méǵh₂- derivation an older theory. No *menegʰ- lexeme in the lexicon: unmapped.
cq1 scan 6: as meinic (EDPC p0279 *menekki-; not *méǵh₂s).

cq1 scan 24: the table's múin is Kaikki Old Irish muin 'upper back' (< *mon- 'neck') and EModIr. (do) mhúin 'taught' (múinid); the automatic chain matched the homonym *mon- 'man, human being' (Germanic *mann-), which continues neither. No 'neck' *mon- lexeme in the lexicon: unmapped.
